newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota's Humphrey says tobacco pact "woefully inadequate".
newsitem.headline: Minnesota's Humphrey says tobacco pact "woefully inadequate".

text.p: Minnesota Attorney General Hubert Humphrey III said a proposed agreement covering litigation between the tobacco industry and 40 U.S. states was "woefully inadequate."
Humphrey pledged to continue Minnesota's efforts to secure compensation for tobacco-related illnesses.
"The agreement as I understand it is woefully inadequate," Humphrey told a news conference at the state capital here. "The negotiators did a good job but we have a lot further to go," he added.
He said he would carefully monitor how Congress evaluates the agreement.
"It is most important to see how the deal looks after the tobacco-controlled Congress has acted," he said.
"We are fully prepared for trial. The court proceedings are going ahead," he said.
In 1994, Minnesota filed suit against the tobacco industry seeking compensation for public funds spent to treat tobacco-related illnesses. The trial is scheduled to begin in January 1998.
